title: Happy 100th Birthday to David Attenborough, the Voice of the Wild!
summary:
Can you imagine turning 100 years old and still being the most famous wildlife explorer on Earth? That's David Attenborough, and today is his birthday! For over 70 years, he's been the excited, hushed voice behind nature shows that take us to jungles, mountains, and deep oceans—all from our living rooms.

Attenborough didn't just show pretty animals. He made sure every fact was scientifically correct, teaching millions about evolution and animal behavior. But as he saw climate change and plastic pollution hurting the planet, he started speaking out. "He is showing you the majesty, the ferocity, the fragility of the natural world," says Professor Ben Garrod, a biologist. Attenborough felt he had to warn us because leaders weren't acting fast enough.

Even though he's super famous, Attenborough doesn't like the spotlight. His friend and producer Alastair Fothergill says Attenborough always reminds his team: "Remember, the animals are the stars, I'm not." One of his most famous moments was in 1979, when a baby gorilla sat on him and tried to take off his shoes. He just laughed, speechless with joy.

Born in 1926, young David loved collecting fossils and snake skins on bike rides. That curiosity led him to study science and eventually make TV history. Today, cinemas are playing his films, and scientists everywhere are thanking him for showing us why nature is worth saving.
why_it_matters: Attenborough's work helps kids see how amazing nature is and why it needs care, so they can grow up to love and protect the planet.

background_read: Sir David Attenborough is a British naturalist and broadcaster who made wildlife documentaries for the BBC (the British Broadcasting Corporation, a public TV network) starting in the 1950s.
His most famous series include 'Life on Earth' and 'Planet Earth', which used new camera technology to film animals like never before.
Attenborough has been knighted by the Queen, so his full title is Sir David Attenborough, but he usually prefers to be called David.
Article_Structure: WHO: Sir David Attenborough, the world-famous wildlife broadcaster and nature expert.
WHAT: Celebrating his 100th birthday by looking back at his career teaching about evolution, warning about climate change, and creating iconic moments like a baby gorilla playing with his shoes.
WHERE: His documentaries have taken viewers everywhere—from jungles to deep oceans—but the celebration is global, with cinemas playing his films.
WHY: To honour his life-long dedication to showing the beauty and fragility of the natural world and to inspire action to protect it.

perspectives.description: Attenborough is a hero who has opened millions of eyes to the wonders of wildlife and made science exciting and important.
Some believe he waited too long to speak out strongly about climate change, but now his voice is one of the most powerful calling for action.
His documentaries shaped how we view nature and conservation, blending scientific accuracy with a deep love for the living world.
